name: Boot stage: CLI flags and per-profile userData folders
what: The app starts through a tiny boot script that parses command-line flags and picks an isolated user-data folder before the main bundle loads. Developers and QA can run separate profiles (dev environment, dev mode, integration test) side by side with the real install.
how: boot.bundle.cjs parses flags with command-line-args style option lists (--startup, --logLevel, --resourcePath, --devEnv, --jsPath, --proxy-server, --troubleshoot, --userAgent, --bootClient, --fragments). It calls app.setPath("userData") to Slack, SlackDevEnv, SlackDevMode, SlackIntegrationTest or SlackUserData (UNC-redirect case) and then requires main.bundle.cjs. Insecure Chromium flags (disable-web-security, allow-running-insecure-content) make the process exit.
evidence: slack/dist/boot.bundle.cjs#c55105 Windows toast COM launch argument stripped
verevonRelevance: A native or agent-host shell for Verevon should isolate dev/test profiles from the real profile from day one; today Verevon is a web SPA with no local profile.
notes: Quality 4: simple, defensive (rejects insecure flags), but standard Electron practice. Offsets are JS char indexes (see deep.md).

name: Single-instance lock with protocol-activation sanity check and focus steal
what: Launching Slack a second time (or clicking a slack:// link) hands the request to the running instance instead of starting another one, and the window comes to the foreground.
how: Module 41235 requests the Electron single-instance lock when packaged and not a Squirrel event; if the lock fails the process quits. A guard aborts when a protocol activation arrives with unexpected extra arguments (slack: plus /p plus more than 3 args). When a protocol URL is present it runs rundll32 User32.dll,SetFocus to defeat Windows focus-stealing prevention. The Windows toast COM activator CLSID differs per distribution (Store, MSIX, Squirrel).
evidence: slack/dist/main.bundle.cjs#c1436543 focus steal on protocol launch
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a desktop wrapper, deep links into a Space must route to the existing window; copy the "validate activation args before acting" guard.

name: slack:// protocol registration across Win32, MSIX and macOS
what: Slack registers itself as the handler for slack:// links so links in browsers, emails and other apps open the right workspace, channel or action.
how: Non-MSIX: app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient("slack") (a dev/chromedriver variant passes --test-type=webdriver). MSIX: AppxManifest declares uap3:Protocol Name="slack" with Parameters "/p \"%1\"". macOS: app.on("open-url"), which relaunches into a dev environment when the URL matches devEnv=(dev|staging|qa). A StartupTask "SlackStartup" and an app-execution alias are also declared.
evidence: install:C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/com.tinyspeck.slackdesktop_4.52.178.0_x64__8yrtsj140pw4g/AppxManifest.xml (windows.protocol, windows.startupTask, windows.appExecutionAlias, comServer toast activation)
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a link grammar (verevon://space/<id>?thread=...) and the Space UI must actually consume thread deep links, which today are generated but ignored.
notes: AppxManifest was read from the installed package (program metadata, read-only).

name: Deep-link grammar and parser (channel, open, app, setting, login-v2, magic-login, toolbelt-callback)
what: One URL scheme drives many things: open a workspace or channel, run an app action, change a setting, sign in several workspaces at once, finish a magic-link login, or complete a developer OAuth.
how: oe() parses slack://<cmd>?args into {args:{...searchParams, cmd:host}, pathname}. Dedicated matchers exist for slack://setting (JSON payload), slack://app (actions), slack://login-v2 (indexed token sets 0.host/0.tokens/0.dpop, 1.host ...), /magic-login/<TEAM>-token paths, slack://toolbelt-callback (OAuth code/state), slack://noop, devEnv=..., openDevToolsOnStart and feature_*=1 / pri=N webapp params. host params must pass a Slack-domain check or are dropped ("received bad host param").
verevonRelevance: Define an explicit, validated deep-link grammar for Verevon Spaces (space, thread, run, approval) and reject unknown hosts/params the way Slack does.
notes: Scout listed only 5 links; login-v2, magic-login and setting payloads are additional.

name: Deep links are resolved to the user's own workspace and forwarded to the web app
what: A slack:// link that names a team is mapped to a workspace the signed-in user actually belongs to, then handed to the web app, which opens the right thing. Links arriving before the web app has loaded are held and delivered afterwards.
how: Epics TRANSFORM_DEEP_LINKS (re-writes the team parameter through userWorkspaces membership) and FORWARD_DEEP_LINK_TO_WEBAPP (waits for WEBAPP_LOADED, 10 s timeout, then main->renderer IPC FORWARD_DEEP_LINK). The preload calls window.desktopDelegate.handleDeepLinkWithArgs, or window.desktopDelegates[teamId] for a specific workspace.
verevonRelevance: Space links should be authorised against Control membership before navigation (never widen ACL); the "resolve then forward, queue until ready" pattern fits Verevon.

name: Settings can be changed by deep link, but only through a validated allowlist
what: Support and docs can send a slack://setting link that flips selected desktop settings (for example release channel or hardware acceleration) without the user digging through menus.
how: UPDATE_SETTINGS_VIA_DEEP_LINKS parses the JSON payload, picks only keys in the f7 allowlist (31 keys), validates with the Joi schema dl, and rejects clientEnvironment changes and unknown release channels. Related epics switch client feature mode via deep link, magic link or sign-out.
evidence: slack/dist/main.bundle.cjs#c1112092 JSON parse with warn on failure
verevonRelevance: A "support link" to flip a Verevon workspace flag is useful but must go through the same allowlist + schema discipline, and never touch org-level policy.
notes: Risk: any app that can launch slack:// can change those settings; the allowlist is what contains it.

name: App-action deep links (reset window, quit, reveal logs, clear cache and restart)
what: Links such as slack://app/?action=reset-window run local housekeeping actions. The Windows jump list uses the same link to offer "Move Slack to current display".
how: tT.gM enum maps action names to dispatches (QUIT_APP, REVEAL_LOGS, RESET_WINDOW, CLEAR_CACHE_AND_RESTART). APP_ACTIONS_VIA_DEEP_LINKS epic is feature-gated (appActionsViaDeepLinks).
verevonRelevance: Low priority; useful only as a pattern for "repair my client" links in support flows.
notes: Whether appActionsViaDeepLinks is enabled in production cannot be read offline.

name: Windows jump list with recent workspaces and a display-recovery task
what: Right-clicking the taskbar icon lists up to ten workspaces (opens straight into each) and a "Move Slack to current display" task.
how: gf class builds app.setJumpList with a Workspaces custom category (slack://open?team=<id> tasks) and a Tasks category; refreshed when workspaces or locale change; honours removedItems.
verevonRelevance: Quick-jump to a Space from the OS shell (jump list/dock menu) is a cheap, high-value native touch if Verevon wraps the web UI.

name: Tray icon with three states, tooltip counts and a launch-control menu
what: A system-tray icon shows rest / unread / highlight states, a tooltip like "You have 3 notifications", and a right-click menu to pick a workspace, toggle Launch on Login, choose Show immediately vs Keep in background, check for updates, open Preferences or quit.
how: gg tray handler derives icon + tooltip from aggregated unreads (getTrayStateFromUnreadsInfo: highlights>0 => "highlight" icon and number; unreads>0 => "unread" with optional bullet), uses slack-taskbar-{rest,unread,highlight}.ico (macOS template PNGs), ICU plural tooltips, and a menu built from the workspace list. Tray state also carries isRecording and launchEnforced.
verevonRelevance: Aggregate "needs-you" count across Spaces and agents for tray/badge; Verevon has only per-room dots today.

name: Tray click is flag-gated: foreground the app, or summon the "command center"
what: With the desktop_command_center flag on, a left-click on the tray raises the main window and opens a quick overlay in the web app (log text calls it "Slackbot Mini"); right-click shows the menu. With the flag off, a click simply foregrounds Slack.
how: handleSlackbotMiniClick (200 ms throttled) calls ar() (forceAllowFocus native call, else setAlwaysOnTop trick on Win10 build >= 15000) and sends NOTIFY_GLOBAL_SHORTCUTS_TRIGGER with feature desktop_command_center to the MAIN window web contents. It does not open a separate native window.
verevonRelevance: An always-available agent entry (tray + global hotkey opening an in-app overlay) maps directly to a Verevon "ask my agent" quick surface.
notes: CORRECTS inventory: the scout described a separate Slackbot Mini window; code shows an overlay rendered by the web app inside the main window.

name: Taskbar overlay badge from 101 pre-rendered PNGs, counting highlights across all workspaces
what: The Windows taskbar icon shows a red number overlay (1-99, then 99+) for notifications that need attention, summed over every signed-in workspace.
how: SET_BADGE_EPIC recomputes iL(webapp.teams).unreadHighlights on redux changes and window foreground, then calls BrowserWindow.setOverlayIcon with a nativeImage created from base64 PNGs in resources/unreads-badge/unread-badge-resources.json (index 0-100); accessibility label "You have unread messages".
verevonRelevance: Ship one aggregate attention counter (mentions + approvals needing the human + agent questions) for the OS badge; pre-rendering avoids canvas work in the shell.
notes: Counts highlights only; plain unreads change the tray icon but not the number.

name: Taskbar flash behaviour (idle vs always) with an explanatory balloon
what: When a notification arrives the taskbar button can flash once after 10 idle seconds (default) or whenever active; if the user closes the window and the app keeps running, a tray balloon explains why Slack did not quit.
how: Settings win32.windowFlashBehavior ("idle"|"always"), FLASH_WINDOW_ON_NOTIFICATION epic, showBalloon kinds window-flash and run-from-tray, with hasExplainedWindowFlash to show the balloon once.
evidence: https://slack.com/help/articles/201355156-Configure-your-Slack-notifications (DOC: one flash after 10 idle seconds by default)
verevonRelevance: Explaining "why the app is still running" the first time is a good trust pattern for background agent hosts.
notes: DOC cross-check agrees with the default.

name: Native application menu with Alt-mnemonics that open sub-menus from the keyboard
what: Menus (File, Edit, View, Go, Conversation, History, Window, Help, Developer) exist natively; on Windows with the custom title bar, Alt+F/E/V/G/C/H open the matching menu from the keyboard and workspaces are bound to Ctrl+1..9.
how: fw class builds the template from ordered items (menu extension API adds items), shows it through POPUP_APP_MENU with invokedViaKeyboard; buildTeamMenuItem sets accelerator CmdOrCtrl+N for the first 9 workspaces. Menu usage is tracked by trackMenuEvent.
verevonRelevance: Keyboard parity (workspace/Space switching by number, F6 region cycling) is table stakes for power users; Verevon should specify it.

name: Custom window chrome rendered as a web component, themed by the selected workspace
what: On Windows/macOS the title bar is not the OS one: it is a web-rendered strip whose colours come from the active workspace's sidebar theme, with window controls and an app-menu button.
how: BrowserWindow frame:false with titleBarStyle hidden + titleBarOverlay (33 px, transparent). The preload injects an inlined "windowchrome" bundle through webFrame.executeJavaScript that defines <window-chrome> and <button is="window-chrome-app-menu">; state (maximize, fullscreen, title, titleBar colours from team.theme.titlebarBackground/TextColor, default #232323) comes from a selector over the shell redux store.
verevonRelevance: Workspace/org-themed shell chrome reinforces which tenant a user is acting in; consider a visible tenant colour band in the Verevon header.
notes: Gated by isWin10 or the window-chrome debug feature on non-Win10.

name: Window bounds persistence, display validation and display-scale healing
what: The window reopens where it was, but is pulled back on-screen if a monitor disappeared; after docking/undocking, resume or unlock the DPI/scale is re-applied so the UI does not stay blurry or mis-sized.
how: validateBoundsForDisplay clamps saved mainWindowSettings.bounds to a display work area (with 1.2x tolerance); HEAL_DISPLAY_SCALE epic debounces 15 s and re-applies scale on display, resume and unlock events for MAIN/WEBAPP windows; jump-list/menu task moves the window to the current display.
verevonRelevance: Only matters if Verevon ships a native shell; note the cost of multi-monitor and DPI bugs.

name: Main-process window drag loop for frameless windows
what: Dragging the custom title bar moves the window smoothly even on high-DPI multi-monitor setups.
how: START_WINDOW_DRAG / STOP_WINDOW_DRAG IPC: main records the cursor grab offset and runs an 8 ms setInterval that calls setBounds from screen.getCursorScreenPoint(), cleaning up on close.
verevonRelevance: None for a web SPA; relevant only if a Tauri/Electron shell adopts frameless windows.
notes: Workaround for -webkit-app-region limits; polling at 8 ms is CPU-visible.

name: Allow-listed remote calls on BrowserWindow and window events from the web app
what: The web UI can minimise, maximise, set always-on-top, resize, flash, show progress and listen to a few window events, but only through a fixed whitelist of methods.
how: EXEC_BROWSERWINDOW_METHOD takes (windowId, method, ...args); methods must be in a ~90-name allowlist (yM) else "cannot be called on a BrowserWindow". REGISTER/UNREGISTER_EVENT_LISTENER permits only moved and will-move and auto-cleans on destroyed/render-process-gone/did-navigate. Preload exposes callBrowserWindowMethod and subscribeToFrameStateChanges.
verevonRelevance: A reusable "capability allowlist" idea: web code gets a named set of host operations, never raw handles. Mirrors Verevon's rule that the Model proposes, a trusted executor disposes.

name: Web-initiated native child windows with an option allowlist and a minimal preload
what: Pop-outs (for example call windows) are real native windows opened by the web app, sized and positioned from options it supplies, but only recognised options are honoured and the child gets almost no native bridge.
how: setWindowOpenHandler parses frameName options, keeps only keys in fT (width, height, x, y, frame, alwaysOnTop, titleBarStyle, vibrancy, ... 40 keys) plus titleBarOverlay/trafficLight shorthands, attaches parentId, forces the hardened webPreferences and child-preload-entry-point.bundle.js. The child preload only exposes slackPlatform.isWayland and zoom handling, and only when the opener is a trusted Slack origin.
verevonRelevance: Good template for letting an agent browser/computer panel open pop-out windows with capped options and no host bridge.
notes: Quality 5: least-privilege applied consistently (options, preload, webPreferences).

name: Server-driven auto-update decision ("should-i-update") with hourly checks
what: The desktop app asks a Slack endpoint whether it should update, sending platform, version, OS, channel and installer type. Checks run hourly and on demand from the menu; the menu item shows Checking / Downloading / An update is available / Restart to Apply Update.
how: GET {base}/desktop/update/v2/should-i-update?platform&version&os_version&channel[&os_product&servicing_channel][&arch=arm64]&updater_variant=msix|squirrel[&is_user_initiated=1]. The JSON reply (update_available, version, url, why[]) drives the Squirrel or MSIX updater. AUTO_UPDATE_TIMER fires every 36e5 ms; MANUAL_UPDATE_CHECK is gated on the main window being ready. On endpoint failure the client reports update_available=false with the error in why[].
verevonRelevance: Server-side rollout control (cohort, channel, OS) beats a static feed; a Verevon native shell should ask Control/Model plane "should I update" rather than polling a file.
notes: Quality 5: decision logic lives on the server; client is thin, observable (desktop_updater_* traces) and failure-safe.

name: Signed update-URL override for testing (RSA-SHA256 plus freshness window)
what: Engineers can point the updater at a test server by environment variable, but only with a valid signature that is fresh relative to process start.
how: SLACK_UPDATE_URL is honoured only if SLACK_UPDATE_URL_SIGNATURE verifies (RSA-SHA256 over the URL and the SLACK_UPDATE_URL_SIGNATURE_TS timestamp against an embedded public key) and the timestamp is within 5 hours (18e6 ms) of the process creation time.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon override path (dev feed, staging model gateway) should require a signed, expiring token rather than a plain env var.
notes: The public key is embedded in the bundle (public material, not reproduced here).

name: Platform-specific update engines: Squirrel with a RELEASES pre-check and MSIX re-registration
what: Per-user installs update through Squirrel.Windows; Store/MSIX installs update by re-registering the package and restarting the app safely.
how: WindowsSquirrelUpdater first fetches {updateUrl}/RELEASES, picks the highest valid semver and compares it to the running version before calling autoUpdater.setFeedURL/checkForUpdates. WindowsMsixUpdater.quitAndInstall calls native app.registerRestart (NoCrash|NoHang|NoReboot flags) and app.registerPackage(familyName,{forceShutdown:true}) from slack-desktop-utils, then app.quit(). Squirrel first-run and uninstall hooks are handled in a lazily loaded chunk (863.bundle.cjs).
evidence: slack/node_modules/@tinyspeck/slack-desktop-utils/lib/index.js:142 native wrapper restart-flag constants (registerRestart/registerPackage are native exports)
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships MSIX/Squirrel, copy the idea of querying native restart registration so Windows relaunches the app after an update.

name: Update success tracking via nextExpectedMinAppVersion and launch-failure attribution
what: After an update is applied, the app remembers which version it expects to become; if the new build crashes at launch, that is reported as an update failure rather than a generic crash.
how: Local setting nextExpectedMinAppVersion is read by the fatal-exception handler; on crash it emits desktop_updater_fail (update_fail_type app_launch_fail, expected min version) via both track() and trace(), clears the marker, flushes telemetry and offers Close/Restart/Restart & Report. An UPDATE_SUCCESS_TRACKING epic also exists (body not read).
verevonRelevance: Tie crash/regression telemetry to the release that was just rolled out; relevant for any Verevon agent-host auto-update.

name: Release channels (prod, beta, dogfood) switchable at runtime
what: Users or admins can move a client to the beta channel (and Slack staff to dogfood); a banner confirms "You've been added to the beta" and the app immediately receives that channel's updates.
how: Enum Xp = dogfood|beta|prod; user-selectable subset beta|prod; setting releaseChannelOverride (win32/darwin); a SWITCH_UPDATE_CHANNELS epic reacts to channel switches (body not read); the channel is a query parameter on the update endpoint and a tag in telemetry. Can be set by slack://setting deep link, by IT policy (ReleaseChannel) or through UPDATE_SETTINGS.
verevonRelevance: Channels per org (stable/beta) managed by Control policy would let Verevon canary a shell or Space UI to staff first.

name: Launch-at-login that respects machine policy and the MSIX StartupTask
what: "Launch on login" is a checkbox, but if IT enforces launch through the machine registry the user cannot turn it off, and Store builds use the Windows StartupTask API instead of registry Run keys.
how: Module 6440 inspects login items for Slack.exe, the Squirrel stub and Update.exe in user vs machine scope, cleans duplicate user entries, treats machine scope as enforced (launchEnforced shown disabled in the tray menu); MSIX path uses systemPreferences.getStartupTaskState/enableStartupTask/disableStartupTask with EnabledByPolicy/DisabledByPolicy handling; hideOnStartup chooses Show immediately vs Keep in background.
verevonRelevance: Org-enforced settings should be visible as locked (not hidden) in Verevon's own settings UI.

name: Four-layer managed configuration read from the registry, macOS managed prefs and /etc
what: IT can lock or default desktop settings per machine: AutoUpdate, ReleaseChannel, ClientEnvironment, DefaultSignInTeam, DownloadPath, HardwareAcceleration, HideOnStartup, SignInMethod and WebSwitches. "Policy" values are locked; "Defaults" are starting values users may change.
how: Windows: registry-js enumerates HKLM then HKCU under SOFTWARE\Policies\Slack (policy) and ...\Slack\Defaults (defaults), HKLM wins. macOS: cf-prefs isPreferenceForced/getPreferenceValue (policy) and a "Defaults" dictionary. Linux: JSON file /etc/slack-desktop.conf with root keys (policy) and "defaults". Each value is validated with the setting's Joi schema. The settings reducer merges slackDefaults < itDefaults < userChoices < itPolicy so policy always wins.
evidence: https://slack.com/help/articles/11906214948755-Manage-desktop-app-configurations (DOC: same keys, paths and HKLM>HKCU precedence)
verevonRelevance: Mirror this: org policy from Control (locked) > org defaults > user choice > product defaults, with the UI told which keys are enforced (see _enforced).
notes: Quality 5: three OS mechanisms behind one typed interface, schema-validated, documented publicly, cross-verified with DOC.

name: Typed user-settings store with a built-in Settings Editor window
what: Advanced desktop settings (notifications, zoom, theme, tray, spellcheck, scrollbars, flash behaviour) are stored in one validated object, and a hidden "Settings Editor" window shows every row with its effective value and which layer set it.
how: Joi schema dl lists the user-changeable keys; settings reducer keeps four layers; SHOW_SETTINGS_EDITOR opens a component window (settings-editor.html + bundle, CSP + SRI) with a table of settings rows; deep link and web app can call UPDATE_SETTINGS with a layer argument.
verevonRelevance: A "why is this setting what it is" inspector (default/org/user/policy) is a strong supportability feature for Verevon admins.

name: Web UI is told which settings are IT-enforced
what: The web app can grey out controls that IT has locked, because the shell exposes the list of enforced keys.
how: The preload selector for settings returns {..., _enforced: Object.keys(settings.itPolicy)} through window.desktop.redux.getState("settings"); only an allowlisted subset of settings, app state, environment and window frames is mirrored to the web app.
verevonRelevance: Same contract Verevon needs between Control policy and the SPA: ship "locked_by_policy" with each effective value.

name: Local shortcuts: numpad zoom, F6/Tab region cycling forwarded as synthetic key events
what: Keyboard users can cycle between app regions with F6 / Shift+F6 and tab order, and zoom with Ctrl +/- including the numpad.
how: LOCAL_SHORTCUT epic hooks before-input-event for NumpadAdd/NumpadSubtract (preventDefault then ZOOM_IN/OUT); FOCUS_INPUT_EVENTS translates NEXT_SECTION/PREVIOUS_SECTION menu commands into webContents.sendInputEvent F6 (shift for previous) and Tab; preload intercepts Ctrl+= for zoom.
verevonRelevance: Region cycling (F6) is an accessibility baseline Verevon should specify for the cockpit tabs and the room pulse rail.

name: Zoom model: Ctrl +/-/0, clamped levels, pinch disabled
what: Zoom steps are controlled by the app (not Chromium pinch) so layouts stay predictable, and the web app receives a --zoom-factor CSS variable.
how: Switch disable-pinch plus webFrame.setVisualZoomLevelLimits(1,1) in the preload; zoomLevel reducer clamps -3..5 and maps to factors (1, 1.1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2 above 0; 0.9, 0.8, 0.7 below); preload sets document.body --zoom-factor on resize.
verevonRelevance: Low relevance; note that CSS-driven density modes are an alternative to browser zoom.

name: Theme handling: user theme, system-theme sync, high contrast and reduced transparency
what: The shell follows the OS dark/light and high-contrast settings if the user enables sync, and disables vibrancy/material effects when the OS asks for reduced transparency.
how: Settings userTheme (default light), systemThemeSyncEnabled, shouldUseHighContrastColors (nativeTheme.shouldUseHighContrastColors observed), nativeTheme "updated" listener updating systemTransparency, background/vibrancy/backgroundMaterial computed per platform in lD().
verevonRelevance: Verevon already ships themes in the SPA; the OS-level hooks only matter for a native shell.

name: Localisation: 9 shell languages x 6 string namespaces with ICU plurals, 12 web locales
what: Menus, dialogs and tray text are translated into German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Chinese; the web app has 12 locale variants (adds en-GB, es-LA, pt-BR, zh-TW) and the shell follows the locale the web app reports.
how: resources/locales/<lang>/desktop_{browser,external,general,menu,messagebox,renderer}_en_GB.json (hash-keyed ICU messages, e.g. plural tooltips); LOAD_LOCALE and GET_LOCALE_RESOURCE IPC give the web app the same loader; APPLY_LOCALE_FROM_WEBAPP re-applies locale and dispatches settings; MSIX manifest declares 10 language resources; build uses @tinyspeck/i18n-translation-tools and a lint:locales script.
evidence: install:C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/com.tinyspeck.slackdesktop_4.52.178.0_x64__8yrtsj140pw4g/AppxManifest.xml (Resources: EN DE FR ES JA IT KO PT-BR ZH-CN ZH-TW)
verevonRelevance: Verevon i18n is partial (activity grammar labels are hard-coded Norwegian); adopt message-id based ICU strings across the Space UI and any native shell.

name: Accessibility plumbing: OS screen-reader detection, high contrast, keyboard-opened menus
what: The shell detects when assistive technology is on, tells the web app, and exposes menus to the keyboard.
how: app accessibilitySupportEnabled is observed (ACCESSIBILITY_SUPPORT_CHANGED), forwarded to window.desktopDelegate.accessibilitySupportChanged, and reported as telemetry; NOTIFY_DELEGATE_ACCESSIBILITY epic; keyboard-invoked app menu (Alt+letter); high-contrast flag passed to the web app.
verevonRelevance: Track screen-reader prevalence and test the Space cockpit tablist with it; Verevon already has roving arrow-key tabs.

name: Self-service support kit: net log, verbose logs, GPU page, tracing UI, cache reset, reset app data
what: A built-in Developer/Troubleshooting menu lets support capture network logs, restart with verbose logging, open chrome://gpu, show the tracing UI, clear cache and exit, toggle hardware acceleration, copy the installation ID, open the crash-dump folder, or wipe all app data.
how: Menu ids menuitem-net-log, menuitem-clear-cache, menuitem-copy-installation-id, menuitem-reset-app-data, ELECTRON_DEBUG_LOG; net-log window (net-log-window.html) driven by RESTART_WITH_NET_LOG/START_NET_LOG; OPEN_GPU_INFO loads chrome://gpu (blocked for MSIX); a --troubleshoot CLI flag exists (boot calls app.exit; the troubleshooter itself is not in this bundle); reset-app-data confirms with "This will sign you out from all of your workspaces".
verevonRelevance: A "Support bundle" action (redacted logs + settings layers + feature flags) should exist for Verevon agent hosts and the SPA.
notes: Quality 4 (high end): unusually complete self-service diagnostics, but mostly assembled from standard Chromium tools.

name: Per-surface rotating logs, console capture with truncation, and log upload to support
what: Each window type (main web app, service worker, notification window, pickers) logs its console to its own rotating file; support can upload a zip of logs and state from the app.
how: l9() subscribes to webContents console-message and writes through a logger instance with an identifier per webContents type, maxFiles 10 when webapp-extended-logs is on, messages over 131072 chars truncated; service worker console is captured separately; uploadAppLogsArchive zips files and POSTs to the profiling.addLogging API with platform=ssb.
verevonRelevance: Log capture per surface with redaction at export is the model for Verevon's agent-run diagnostics.

name: Crash and hang handling: fatal-exception dialog, unresponsive dialog, call-stack hashing
what: If the main process throws, the app flushes telemetry and shows Close / Restart / Restart & Report issue; if the web UI hangs it offers Wait, Reload or Restart.
how: rz crash handler ("ABOUT TO QUIT DUE TO FATAL JAVASCRIPT EXCEPTION") skips a short list of benign messages (net::err_, notification cache), flushes telemetry, saves reportIssueOnStartup, relaunches. webContentsTimeoutDialogEpic waits 5 s (15 s with extended_unresponsive_timeout flag), captures the renderer JS call stack, tags Sentry with an md5 of the top frames, and records whether the system just resumed from sleep.
verevonRelevance: Hashing hang stacks and tagging "just resumed from sleep" turns noisy hang reports into actionable buckets.
notes: Quality 5: recovery plus attribution.

name: Crash-integrity check: detect the app binary being replaced while running
what: If the executable on disk changes (for example an update lands) and a child process then crashes, the crash is tagged as an integrity failure instead of a product bug and can trigger a clean restart.
how: INTEGRITY_CHECK epic stores Slack.exe mtime at launch; on child-process-gone/render-process-gone (throttled 60 s) it compares the mtime again; mismatch emits desktop_integrity_check_failed, sets Sentry flag integrity.failed and, behind the crash_integrity_check flag, runs the fatal-restart path.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for self-updating hosts: do not let post-update crashes pollute reliability metrics.
notes: CORRECTS inventory: this is a replaced-binary detector, not a tamper check.

name: Distribution classification (Store, MSIX, MSI variants, DDL, MAS) and UA capability tokens
what: The app knows how it was installed and tells the server in the user agent so the web app and update service can behave accordingly.
how: u() returns WinStore, MSIX, MSQ (installInfo present), LMSI (machine-wide "Slack Deployment"), DDL (Update.exe present), MSI or MAS; the UA string appends WindowsStore/x, OS_Product, Servicing_Channel, the distribution token, WindowsOnArm/WoAEmu, " Sonic", " GovEnvironment" and Slack_SSB/<version>. Update endpoint and telemetry carry the same facts.
evidence: https://slack.com/help/articles/212475728-Deploy-Slack-for-Windows (DOC: MSI/MSIX deployment, MSQ prefix means managed updates)
verevonRelevance: A host-capability UA/handshake lets the SPA adapt (for example hide update UI when the host manages updates).

name: Dev/QA affordances shipped in production: feature fragments, devEnv, local assets, debug features
what: Slack staff can point the shipped app at a local web build, a dev environment or toggle debugging aids (React DevTools, OPFS explorer, epic trace, extended web logs, window-chrome).
how: --jsPath/js_path and slack://open?devEnv=... select web sources; TOGGLE_FEATURE_FRAGMENT only honours js_path when not packaged or the devtools flag allows it; USE_LOCAL_ASSETS epic; debugFeatures enum {react-devtools, opfs-explorer, epic-trace, window-chrome, webapp-extended-logs}; an isolated userData profile is used for dev environments; a local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:<random> accepts magic_login_uri POSTs in dev.
verevonRelevance: Dev affordances must be gated by build and policy; Verevon should keep any "run UI from local path" off in production hosts.
notes: The presence of OPFSExplorer is also evidence that the web client stores data in OPFS (see realtime records).

name: Packaging and release pipeline: Forge, Squirrel, MSIX, WiX MSI, notarisation, ASAR tooling
what: One codebase ships as Squirrel installer, MSIX/Store package, machine-wide MSI, macOS DMG/ZIP (signed and notarised) and Linux packages.
how: package.json devDependencies: @electron-forge/core 8.0.0-alpha.8 (maker-dmg/zip), electron-winstaller, electron-windows-msix, electron-wix-msi, @electron/osx-sign, @electron/notarize, @electron/asar, @electron/fuses, @electron/get, @aws-sdk/client-s3 (artefact upload), @octokit/rest, packagecloud CLI script, rspack + swc bundling, jest 30, oxlint, knip, dependency-cruiser; yarn 4 workspaces (spec/e2e, spec/old-joe, tools/triage-agent).
verevonRelevance: None directly; shows the breadth (5 install channels) a native Verevon shell would inherit.
notes: Build-time only; nothing here runs in the shipped app.

name: Multi-workspace switching inside one window (menu, Ctrl+1..9, tray, jump list, touch swipe)
what: All signed-in workspaces live in one window; users switch with the sidebar rail, Ctrl/Cmd+1..9, next/previous commands, the tray menu, the jump list, or a three-finger swipe on touch screens (two-finger swipe goes back/forward).
how: Shell keeps workspaces (id, name, domain, url, icon sizes, order, variant) and workspacesMeta.selectedWorkspaceId; WORKSPACE_SELECTION epic sends SELECT_NEXT/PREVIOUS/BY_ID to the web app, which implements focusNextWorkspace/focusPreviousWorkspace/setFocusedWorkspace on window.desktopDelegate; web app calls desktop.workspaces.sync/selectionChanged/storeUserWorkspaces to keep the shell in sync.
verevonRelevance: Verevon org/Space switching should be addressable from OS chrome and keyboard, not only from the in-app sidebar.
notes: Workspaces share one Chromium session (see session-model record).

name: window.desktop bridge: 30-odd namespaces exposed to the trusted web app, plus per-workspace delegates
what: The remote web client gets a typed native API: windows, accelerators, accessibility, app, calls, clipboard, context menus, diagnostics, dock, downloads, local file search, menus, notices/notifications, recent files, OS search index, screen, spellcheck, stats, teams, workspaces, a read-only redux view and window chrome. The web client registers delegates that the shell calls back.
how: preload.bundle.js builds one object and exposes it with contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("desktop") (also legacy alias window.winssb) together with a reduced "process" {versions, mas, sandboxed}. Trust check: only for https Slack origins on port 443, the app:// error/loading pages, or windows opened by those. Reverse direction: setGlobalDelegate / exposeWorkspaceDelegate(workspaceId, delegate).
verevonRelevance: This is the API shape Verevon would need between a Space UI and a host: small, namespaced, validated; define it before building a shell.
notes: REA recorded context_bridge_apis=1 but could not resolve IPC names; the namespace list comes from reading the preload bundle.

name: Remote-controlled Chromium feature overrides and command-line switches
what: Slack can switch Chromium features on or off on user machines (to dodge platform bugs) without shipping a new build; a hard-coded list of risky features is always disabled.
how: electronFeatureOverrides (stored in local-settings.json, delivered by the web app/server) contains filtered entries {filter, enable_blink_features, disable_blink_features, enable_chrome_features, disable_chrome_features, add_browser_command_line_args}; applied at startup via commandLine.appendSwitch. Always disabled: WebRtcHideLocalIpsWithMdns, HardwareMediaKeyHandling, RequestInitiatorSiteLockEnfocement, WinRetrieveSuggestionsOnlyOnDemand, CalculateNativeWinOcclusion, IntensiveWakeUpThrottling, AllowAggressiveThrottlingWithWebSocket, LogJsConsoleMessages, EnableWatermarkView; ExperimentalJSProfiler is enabled. GET_CHROMIUM_FEATURE_OVERRIDES reports applied vs pending.
verevonRelevance: A remote kill-switch for engine-level behaviour is valuable for a fleet of agent hosts; it must be signed/audited because it widens the blast radius.
notes: Disabling AllowAggressiveThrottlingWithWebSocket and IntensiveWakeUpThrottling shows Slack depends on timely WebSocket handling while backgrounded (INF).

name: Desktop feature flags: hourly poll plus flags pushed by the web app
what: Shell behaviours (command center, focus sessions, native notifications, local file search, loading screen, DND check, COM activation, devtools menu) are toggled by server-side flags that the app refreshes hourly and the web app also pushes in.
how: A loop in main calls v8() every 36e5 ms against the environment base URL ("Error checking features"); CHECK_DESKTOP_FEATURES epic applies the result to settings/slackDefaults and logs the enabled set; teams[].featureFlags arrive via REDUX_UPDATE_FROM_WEBAPP; tk.G(flag,state) reads them. Flag names: devtools, mas_native_platform_sign_in_by_default, force_native_notifications, focus_sessions, desktop_local_file_search, desktop_system_diagnostics, desktop_loading_screen, crash_integrity_check, desktop_command_center, extended_unresponsive_timeout, set_system_notification_playback, async_dnd_check, cookie_persistence_logging, windows_com_activation, tsauthSessionMenuItem.
verevonRelevance: Flag-gate shell capabilities per org via Control; log the effective set at boot (desktop_feature_flags_loaded) for support.
notes: Flag defaults and rollout percentages cannot be read offline.

name: GPU/hardware-acceleration fallbacks and safe-mode command-line switches
what: If hardware acceleration misbehaves users or support can disable it (or enable low-end mode) with one restart; if GPU composition is unavailable the app also drops native notifications to the HTML fallback.
how: useHwAcceleration setting and policy HardwareAcceleration; app.disableHardwareAcceleration at start; SET_COMMAND_LINE_SWITCHES allows only disable-gpu and enable-low-end-device-mode (persisted in local-settings.json appCommandLineSwitches); environment rule mn: isGpuCompositionAvailable=false => notificationMethod=null; disable-renderer-backgrounding is always set.
verevonRelevance: Keep escape hatches small and allowlisted (two switches), exactly as Slack does.

name: Keyboard-layout awareness (WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE) and native-keymap
what: The shell tracks the active keyboard layout so keyboard shortcuts and key-code based features (for example push-to-talk combos) map correctly on non-US layouts.
how: SET_KEYBOARD_LAYOUT epic reads the layout via @tinyspeck/native-keymap and hooks window message 81 (WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE) on Windows, storing settings.keyboardLayout which is mirrored to the web app.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon adds global shortcuts, plan for layout-aware key codes from the start.
notes: Purpose of layout mirroring for the web app is inferred from the ta settings mirror list (INF).

name: Shell state lives in a main-process Redux store, replicated to renderers over one IPC channel
what: All desktop-level state (settings, windows, workspaces, downloads, notifications, update status) has a single owner in the main process; preloads hold read replicas and send actions back.
how: Redux Toolkit store in main; renderers use a forward-to-main middleware that sends every non-local action on ipcRenderer channel "redux-action" (actions with meta.scope "local" and types matching /^@@/ or redux-form are not forwarded); main applies and rebroadcasts. A preload boots its replica synchronously via ipcRenderer.sendSync(GET_REDUX_STATE) (main answers with returnValue = full state), dropping the _persist key. Typed action creators carry meta.logPayload allowlists so logs never contain full payloads.
evidence: REA ev_203fd8477a611ebc60bfe0cfc9cbe73086cc727560325ea5525c44d15e153e7f (analyze_javascript_application, directory, record-and-continue; this session) (REA could only see dynamic channel expressions: literal_channels=0)
verevonRelevance: One authoritative host store + typed action contract is a clean way to keep a multi-window shell consistent; the logPayload allowlist idea suits ZDR-minded logging.
notes: Quality 4. REA found 3 IPC operations but no literal channel; the channel name comes from direct reading.

name: About 150 named redux-observable epics structure the whole shell
what: Every shell behaviour (deep links, notifications, updates, downloads, idle, network, tray, menus, telemetry) is an independently named, independently loggable "epic" reacting to actions.
how: Enum of epic names (INITIALIZE_APPLICATION ... MAIN_WINDOW_CREATED, about 150 entries, e.g. dispatchSleepAndWakeEventsEpic, reloadEmptyPagesEpic, flushPersistorOnStateChangeEpic) merged with combineEpics in two lists (app epics and webcontents epics); each epic is wrapped with error logging (logEpicException) and an optional "epic-trace" debug feature emits rxjs_epic_trace telemetry.
verevonRelevance: Per-behaviour named reactors make long-lived host logic testable and traceable; relevant to Verevon agent-host orchestration (named, traced handlers).
notes: Count from enum entries in the main bundle (INF-free count, about 153).

name: Persisted shell state: root-state.json via redux-persist, local-settings.json, instance/tray UUIDs
what: Settings, workspaces and download history survive restarts; a separate small key-value file keeps low-level flags; each install has stable instance IDs for telemetry.
how: redux-persist with a node-file storage at userData/storage/root-state.json, throttle 8 s, 5 s rehydrate timeout, versioned schema, per-slice whitelist transforms (field-level), writeFailHandler; flushPersistorOnStateChange debounces 5 s on workspace changes. local-settings.json (userData) is a synchronous JSON key-value store (atomic write) for flags such as appCommandLineSwitches, electronFeatureOverrides, nextExpectedMinAppVersion, clientEnvironment. Base64 UUID files provide instance and tray ids; the session id is instance id + timestamp.
verevonRelevance: Keep durable host state small, versioned, throttled and redactable; keep tokens out of it.
notes: Secret-bearing stores (cookies, tokens) were not read.

name: One shared Chromium session for all workspaces; isolated "component" partition for local UI
what: Signing in to several workspaces does not create several isolated browser profiles: they share one cookie jar and storage, while Slack's own HTML windows (about, notifications, settings) run in a separate partition so they can never read workspace cookies.
how: Session helper returns session.defaultSession (id PROD_DEFAULT_SESSION) for the web app, or persist:NORMAL/ALTERNATE(+Dev/DevEnv) partitions in dev; "slack-component" partition for app:// component windows; the permission and IPC gates treat the two sessions differently (component session only accepts app: origin).
evidence: slack/dist/main.bundle.cjs#c1002694 IPC gate keyed on session
verevonRelevance: Shared-session multi-tenancy is cheap but means tenant isolation must be enforced server-side; Verevon's per-org Control decisions already assume that.
notes: Cookie names d and lc appear in monitors; values were not read.

name: Three-state connectivity model (online / slackDown / offline) plus network-quality hints
what: The shell distinguishes "no network" from "Slack is down" and passes connection quality to the web app, which can degrade gracefully.
how: Enum p = online|slackDown|offline set through SET_NETWORK_STATUS (NETWORK_STATUS epic); GET_NETWORK_INFO asks the renderer for navigator.connection.effectiveType/downlink and answers GET_NETWORK_INFO_RESPONSE (also added to telemetry spans as network_connection_type/downlink); REQUEST_EMULATION_THROTTLE (offline, latency, download/upload throughput, connectionType; CPU throttle rate) lets diagnostics emulate bad networks through the debugger.
verevonRelevance: Surface "service down" vs "you are offline" separately in Verevon (today the room silently polls); it changes what the user should do.
notes: How the web client sets slackDown (probably from its WebSocket state) is INF.

name: Activity-driven "tickle" keeps the realtime connection warm while the user is active
what: While the user is active and the screen is unlocked, the shell pings the web app every 10 seconds so it can verify or revive its message connection; after sleep/lock the web app is told immediately.
how: SYSTEM_IDLE_STATUS epic: every 10 s, powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime() <= 20 s means ACTIVE; when ACTIVE and not locked it dispatches TICKLE (FM) which sends TICKLE_MESSAGE_SERVER to every WEBAPP_LOADED webContents; the preload calls window.desktopDelegate.maybeTickleMS(). Idle/locked/awake states are part of the store mirrored to the web app (systemIdleStatus, systemLockedStatus, isMachineAwake).
evidence: slack/dist/preload.bundle.js#c581678 state mirrored to web app
verevonRelevance: Realtime health nudges driven by OS activity are a cheap fix for stale rooms; Verevon's 6 s polling could at least refetch on activity/visibility/resume.
notes: That "message server" means the WebSocket tier is INF; DOC confirms WebSockets over 443.

name: Sleep/wake, lock and thermal throttling signals forwarded to the web app
what: The web client learns when the machine sleeps or wakes (and when the CPU is throttled) so it can resync or lighten work; lock state is mirrored as state.
how: powerMonitor suspend/resume update a suspend-status action; the DISPATCH_SLEEP_AND_WAKE epic then sends SLEEP_AND_WAKE ("sleep" or "wake") to every webContents and the preload dispatches a DOM Event of that name; powerMonitor "speed-limit-change" (throttled 5 s) sends SPEED_LIMIT_CHANGE (value bucketed by 10) to window.desktopDelegate.speedLimitChanged; lock state is tracked separately (systemLockedStatus); an auth-cookie monitor (flag cookie_persistence_logging) logs sleep duration to debug sign-outs after sleep.
evidence: slack/dist/preload.bundle.js#c712470 DOM event dispatch for SLEEP_AND_WAKE
verevonRelevance: Agent-host clients should resync Space state on resume and expose an explicit "resynced at" marker.

name: Reload of blank pages with quadratic backoff, waiting for the network to return
what: If the web app loads as an empty page, the shell retries with growing delays (1 s, 4 s, 9 s ... up to 10 tries) and, if offline, waits until connectivity returns instead of burning retries.
how: RELOAD_EMPTY_PAGES epic counts per-webContents EMPTY_PAGE states; delay = 1000 * n^2 ms when networkStatus is ONLINE, else waits for SET_NETWORK_STATUS ONLINE; then sends RELOAD_DOCUMENT; gives up after 10. A separate load-timeout path shows "Slack is having trouble loading" with Wait / Reload / Restart.
verevonRelevance: Same recipe works for the Space SPA shell (bounded retry, offline-aware); Verevon polling code has no stated backoff.

name: WebContents lifecycle state machine with session-expired and load-timeout states
what: Each web view is tracked through unloaded, loaded, webapp-loaded, empty, failed, timed-out, crashed and session-expired, driving reloads, dialogs and sign-out handling.
how: Enum oV = unloaded | loaded | page-fail-load | empty-page | webapp-loaded | page-closed | render-process-gone | webapp-session-expired | page-load-timed-out; typed contents types app | auth | posts | report_issue and cloud pickers box | dropbox | gdrive | onedrive; PAGE_LOADED vs WEBAPP_LOADED distinguishes DOM load from the app finishing boot (the preload reports it).
verevonRelevance: Make "app ready" a first-class state (not just DOM loaded) in any Verevon host; queue deep links and notifications until then.

name: Local data lifecycle: clear caches on sign-out, keep IndexedDB until the last workspace leaves, handle Electron version changes
what: Signing out wipes caches and service workers, but the local database (IndexedDB) is only wiped when no workspace remains; upgrading or downgrading the Electron runtime keeps or restores cookies and clears code/service-worker caches that could be incompatible.
how: SIGN_OUT_CLEANUP: session.clearData({dataTypes: backgroundFetch, cache, downloads, fileSystems, serviceWorkers, webSQL [+ indexedDB when workspaces is empty]}), removes non-Slack cookies, deletes per-domain dpop-keys files for domains no longer in use and the macOS auth cookie backup. On Electron major upgrade it copies Cookies to StaleCookies-<prev>; on downgrade restores them and deletes the Service Worker folder; any Electron version change deletes Code Cache.
evidence: slack/dist/main.bundle.cjs#c856201 cookie stash across runtime upgrades
verevonRelevance: Explicit data-lifecycle rules per sign-out/upgrade are rare and valuable; Verevon's deletion saga (per-plane receipts) is the server-side analogue, so ensure any local cache is covered by it.
notes: Quality 5: rollback-safe. Whether IndexedDB holds the message cache is INF (web client not available).

name: The web client uses a Service Worker and OPFS (evidence for an offline-capable local cache)
what: Slack's web client appears to cache assets and data locally: the shell captures service-worker console output and ships an "OPFS explorer" debug tool.
how: CAPTURE_SERVICE_WORKER_CONSOLE_OUTPUT logs session.serviceWorkers console messages (version boots) to webapp-service-worker-console; CLEAR_SERVICE_WORKER epic purges it when the client environment changes (GovSlack); debugFeatures contains opfs-explorer; preload sends RESTART_SELF to the service-worker manager if the preload runs twice in one session.
verevonRelevance: Offline-first for Spaces needs a local store plus a queued-send model; note Verevon's content-bound append decisions make offline queues hard.
notes: INF: shell shows the plumbing, not what the SW/OPFS hold. Confidence medium.

name: Telemetry pipeline: batched clog events, span-style traces and an IPC-validation beacon
what: Usage events are buffered for ~70 seconds and sent in small batches; performance and health are sent as spans with hardware, memory and process counts; invalid IPC calls are beaconed separately.
how: track(): ReplaySubject -> bufferTime(70 s) -> chunks whose encodeURIComponent(JSON) < 1500 chars -> POST {base}/clog/track/ (max 50 chunks per window, rest dropped with a warning). trace(): OpenTracing-like span {id, trace_id, name, start/duration micros, tags v_str/v_bool}, auto-tagged ssb_instance_id, platform, arch, dist, app_version, electron_version, os_version, virtualization, network, memory, CPU model/cores, machine model, uptime, JS heap and renderer/utility/GPU process counts, user_id/team_id. IPC schema failures POST to {base}/beacon/ssbipc (3 s timeout, serialised queue). Sentry + Electron crashReporter minidumps run in parallel; selected action payloads are redacted via logPayload.
verevonRelevance: Verevon must keep ZDR: batch locally, send counts not content, and make event allowlists explicit like logPayload.
notes: Quality 4: efficient batching and rich context, but heavy device profiling (CPU model, machine model, virtualization).

name: Startup performance timeline and loading-screen telemetry
what: Boot time is split into rehydrate, window created, DOM ready and web app loaded, and the web app reports how long the loading screen was visible.
how: Phases REHYDRATE=0, MAIN_WINDOW_CREATED=1, WEB_CONTENTS_DOM_READY=2, WEBAPP_LOADED=3 recorded by RECORD_PERFORMANCE_TIMING; window.desktop.stats.timeToPageLoad and timeSpentInPreload expose them; LoadingScreenTelemetry IPC sends start/end/success; desktop_loading_screen flag controls a native loading screen.
verevonRelevance: Define "time to first useful room" as a measured Space SLO with these phases.

name: In-app diagnostics: Chromium trace sessions, perf metrics, DOM counters, network/CPU emulation
what: Support can record a Chromium trace from the app and upload it, read performance metrics and DOM node counters, and emulate slow networks or CPUs.
how: START_DIAGNOSTICS_TRACE takes {identifier, endpoint, token, mode record-until-full|record-continuously|record-as-much-as-possible|trace-to-console, categoryFilter, captureAllProcess, metadata}; window.desktop.stats exposes defaultTraceCategories, performance.enable/disable/getMetrics, getCPUUsage, getMemoryUsage, getAppMetricsV2, getDOMCounters; REQUEST_EMULATION_THROTTLE uses the debugger protocol (Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate, Network.emulateNetworkConditions).
verevonRelevance: Server-initiated trace capture with an upload token is a strong model for debugging field issues in agent hosts (with consent).

name: Web app pushes team-level state into the shell (unreads, theme, flags, recording)
what: The web client tells the shell each workspace's unread counts, sidebar theme, feature flags, notification preferences, recording state and build version; the shell uses it for the tray, badge, menus and title bar.
how: window.desktop.redux.dispatchUpdate -> REDUX_UPDATE_FROM_WEBAPP validated by schema k: teams[teamId]{theme{titlebarBackground,titlebarTextColor}, notificationPrefs{notificationSound,noTextInNotifications,muteSounds}, connectivityPrefs{ntlmCredentialDomains}, featureFlags{}, unreads{unreads,unreadHighlights,showBullet}, locale, isRecording, version, frontendBuildType, userId}.
verevonRelevance: A narrow, schema-validated "client status" push (unread, theme, flags) is the right shape for a Verevon host to drive badge/tray without reading content.

name: No end-to-end encryption or client-side message store in the shell
what: The desktop shell holds no message data and does no end-to-end encryption; message transport and storage are entirely the web client plus Slack servers.
how: Search of main/preload bundles finds no E2EE primitives beyond safeStorage (used for developer tokens) and Chromium cookie encryption (fuse); chat data never appears in the shell redux schema (only counts, names, urls, themes).
evidence: install:C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/com.tinyspeck.slackdesktop_4.52.178.0_x64__8yrtsj140pw4g/app/Slack.exe byte offset 199176568 (Electron fuse sentinel, wire version 1, 9 fuses = 010011001; Chrome/152.0.7977.130 Electron/44.4.5 string present)
verevonRelevance: Slack-class products rely on server-side controls (EKM, retention); Verevon's ZDR and Control decisions are stronger authority primitives than Slack's shell offers.
notes: Absence claim, medium confidence: grep-based; Slack Enterprise Key Management exists server-side (not verified here).

name: DOC: Slack realtime path (WebSockets over 443, Flannel edge cache, lazy loading)
what: The client bootstraps from a snapshot then listens on a WebSocket; Flannel, an edge cache, answers lazy user/channel lookups and cuts boot payload and reconnect storms.
how: WebSockets over port 443 to wss-primary / wss-backup / wss-mobile.slack.com (proxy exemption list); Flannel hosts are routed per team and region; engineering blog reports ~4M simultaneous connections, 600K client queries/s at peak, 7x smaller boot payload at 1.5K users and 44x at 32K users, 5x fewer presence events after pub/sub presence.
verevonRelevance: Lazy-load members/channels behind an edge cache and use pub/sub presence; replace Verevon's full-thread-list-per-poll with incremental sync.
notes: Numbers are from Slack's own engineering post as summarised by the fetch tool; dated but architecture-level.

name: DOC: Socket Mode for apps (WebSocket envelopes with acknowledgements, up to 10 connections)
what: Apps can receive events over a WebSocket instead of public HTTP: connect with an app-level token, ack each envelope, and reconnect on refresh warnings.
how: apps.connections.open returns a short-lived WSS URL; hello message with connection lifetime; envelope_id must be acknowledged or Slack retries; up to 10 concurrent connections per app; refresh_requested / disconnect warnings; debug_reconnects=true for testing.
verevonRelevance: An agent/bot transport for Spaces (outbound WebSocket with envelope acks) avoids public webhooks for on-prem agents.
notes: Platform feature, not shell; included because it is Slack's realtime contract for bots.

name: Notification pipeline: web app NOTIFY -> state gates -> redux action -> native toast or HTML window
what: The web app asks the shell to show a notification; the shell checks the OS notification state, builds a normalised payload and delivers it natively or through its own fallback window.
how: NOTIFY IPC (Joi schema C) -> check u5 (notification display allowed) and ah (DND/quiet hours) -> default id teamId_msg -> mj() builds payload (defaults: groupWindowsNotifications true, silent false, sound none, hasReply false, notifyPosition bottom_right on same_as_app display, max 3 on screen, 6 s timeout, 2 s after-hover timeout) -> NEW_NOTIFICATION epic -> native Windows toast (default) or HTML window. Telemetry events DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED/CLICK/REPLY/ACTION.
verevonRelevance: Define one normalised attention payload (who, where, thread, urgency, actions, trace id) that web, desktop and push channels share.
notes: Quality 5: single normalised payload, gated, observable end to end.

name: Rich native Windows toasts: grouped headers, circular avatar, hero image, inline reply, action buttons
what: Windows notifications are grouped under the workspace name (or channel name), show the sender avatar in a circle, an optional large image, an inline "Reply" text box and custom action buttons; clicking jumps to the exact message or thread.
how: The shell generates ToastGeneric XML (header id/title/arguments, appLogoOverride hint-crop circle, hero image, audio, <input id="replyBox"> + action with hint-inputId) and passes toastXml/id/groupId to Electron's Notification; COM activation (windows_com_activation flag, MSIX CLSID) returns JSON arguments (type notification|action|header) that are Joi-validated and routed; fallback activationType "protocol" uses slack:// launch URIs with &origin=notification.
verevonRelevance: Reply-from-notification and per-thread deep links are what make attention flows productive; Verevon approvals ("approve/deny") would fit toast action buttons.
notes: Quality 5: richest native notification implementation among what was inspected.

name: Reply to a message from the notification without opening the app
what: Typing in the toast reply box sends a reply into the right channel/thread.
how: Toast "reply" event carries userInputs.replyBox; handleForegroundActivation dispatches REPLY_TO_NOTIFICATION {channel, messageId, response, teamId, traceId, threadTimestamp} (logPayload keeps only the response field name) which the web app turns into a message; click dispatches CLICK_NOTIFICATION with the same ids. The notification payload schema also has a hasReply flag that enables the reply box.
verevonRelevance: Quick-reply to an agent question from the OS notification is a direct fit for Verevon human-in-the-loop prompts.

name: Notification failure counter and automatic failover to the in-app HTML notification window
what: If native notifications keep failing, Slack falls back to its own HTML pop-ups and remembers the failover for a week.
how: trackNotificationFailure counts consecutive failures (5 => telemetry desktop_persistence_notification_failure); settings notificationFailover (timestamp) and notificationFailoverEnabled; initialSettingsPayload resets an HTML method back to null when failover is stale; getNotificationWarnings reports FAILOVER_WITHIN_LAST_WEEK.
verevonRelevance: Any channel adapter (push, email, native) needs a health counter and a fallback ladder; log it for support.

name: HTML notification window: own stacking, corner/display choice, click-through shape, strict CSP + SRI
what: The fallback notification UI is a transparent, always-on-top, non-focusable window anchored to a screen corner on the same or primary display, stacking up to the configured count and auto-dismissing.
how: Component window app://resources/notifications.html (partition slack-component, component preload, windowType notifications) with SET_NOTIFICATIONS_WINDOW_SHAPE for click-through; settings notifyPosition {corner top_left|top_right|bottom_left|bottom_right, display same_as_app|primary}, notificationMaxItems 1-50, notificationTimeout 250-60000 ms, notificationZoomLevel 0.5-5; page has CSP (script-src sha384 hash, frame-src none, img-src slack-edge/slack-imgs/app) and bundles DOMPurify with Trusted Types.
verevonRelevance: None for web; a native shell would need the same fallback ladder.

name: Respecting OS attention state: Windows notifier state, Focus Assist, GPU composition, with isolation in utility processes
what: Slack does not show or sound notifications when Windows has them off (for the app, the user, group policy or manifest), when Focus Assist/quiet hours is on (unless Slack is a priority app), or when the GPU compositor is unavailable.
how: Native getNotifierState (slack-desktop-utils) and getFocusAssist/isPriority(AUMID) (windows-focus-assist) run in short-lived utilityProcess/worker entry points (call-get-windows-notifier-state-..., call-get-windows-focus-assist-...) so a hung COM call cannot block main; u3() applies different rules for "notification display" and "sound playback"; notificationPresentationCheck=false bypasses checks; desktop_notifier_state_* traces record failures.
verevonRelevance: Honour OS Focus/DND for Verevon desktop alerts and isolate flaky native calls from the main loop.
notes: Quality 5: process-isolated native probes with timeouts.

name: Notification health report ("why am I not getting notifications") with cached warnings
what: The web app can ask the shell for a list of reasons notifications may not appear (quiet hours, disabled by policy, no GPU composition, zero timeout, unknown method, recent failover, failover disabled) to show a fix-it banner.
how: getNotificationWarnings: cache TTL 30 s when warnings exist, 1 h when clean; codes include QUIET_HOURS, AC_* notifier states, GPU_COMPOSITION_UNAVAILABLE, ZERO_MAX, ZERO_TIMEOUT, UNKNOWN_METHOD, FAILOVER_WITHIN_LAST_WEEK, FAILOVER_DISABLED (+ mac NOT_DETERMINED); exposed as window.desktop.notice.getNotificationWarnings and included in exported diagnostics.
verevonRelevance: A self-diagnosing attention channel ("alerts blocked by Focus mode") is a differentiator Verevon can copy cheaply.

name: Sound system: 13 named sounds, web vs system playback, packaged sounds for MSIX, 9 call sounds
what: Users choose among named notification sounds; playback can be done by the web app ("web") or by Windows ("system"); call events have their own sound pack.
how: Enum of mp3 names (animal_stick, b2, been_tree, boop, complete_quest_requirement, confirm_delivery, flitterbug, here_you_go_lighter, hi_flowers_hit, hummus, item_pickup, knock_brush, save_and_checkout) shared between schemas; MSIX toasts reference ms-appx:///app/resources/<sound>, non-MSIX toasts are silent and the web app plays audio; SHOULD_PLAY_SOUND answers based on notifier state/Focus Assist; set_system_notification_playback flag sets playback to system once for MSIX; dist contains 9 calls_*_v2.mp3 files.
verevonRelevance: Distinct, user-selectable attention sounds per event class (mention, approval, agent done) improve triage.

name: Focus sessions / DND awareness polled while the app is open
what: When the focus_sessions flag is on, Slack checks the OS focus/DND state on every window focus and every 5 seconds and exposes isInFocusSession to the web app.
how: MONITOR_FOCUS_SESSION epic registers browser-window-focus plus a 5 s loop calling the async DND check (aX/am); state field app.isInFocusSession is mirrored to the preload; asyncDndCheck flag chooses the async implementation.
verevonRelevance: If an agent can interrupt, let it read the user's Focus state before pinging.
notes: macOS DND helper in this build returns false unconditionally (stub); Windows path is real.

name: macOS notification authorisation re-request with throttling
what: If macOS says notification permission was never determined, Slack re-requests it, at most 3 times per session and not more than once per 10 minutes.
how: u4() with promptWhenNotDetermined calls systemPreferences.requestNotificationAuthorization from slack-desktop-utils with session_limit and interval guards and traces desktop_mac_notification_reauthorize.
verevonRelevance: Prompt for permission in context, not on every launch.
notes: macOS-only branch; not exercised on this Windows install.

name: Per-workspace notification preferences mirrored into the shell
what: Each workspace's sound choice, "no text in notifications" privacy setting and mute-sounds flag are pushed from the web app so the native layer obeys them.
how: Schema teams[].notificationPrefs {notificationSound, noTextInNotifications, muteSounds} in REDUX_UPDATE_FROM_WEBAPP; NOTIFY/Notification payloads carry sound, silent, urgency low|normal|critical.
verevonRelevance: Carry a "hide content in notifications" flag per org/user (ZDR-friendly) from day one.

name: DOC: Do Not Disturb, notification schedules, mobile push timing and admin default hours
what: Users pause notifications for a period or on a schedule; mobile push waits until the user is inactive; admins can set default DND hours; colleagues can break through with a once-a-day urgent DM.
how: Desktop: Pause notifications menu or /dnd; schedule every day/weekdays/custom; mobile push default 1 minute after locking the desktop or 10 minutes after cursor inactivity (configurable); default DND hours set by admins at workspace/Grid level; status "Vacationing" turns DND on.
verevonRelevance: Quiet hours/DND (planned S4.4 in Verevon) should include "desktop active so skip mobile push" timing and admin defaults.
notes: Figures from help-center search summaries; older blog said 2 minutes; help center treated as current.

name: DOC: notification preferences (keywords, VIP, per-channel overrides, badges, Activity view)
what: Granular controls: everything vs mentions/DMs, keyword alerts, VIP messages, per-conversation overrides, sounds, hiding previews, badge workspaces, taskbar flashing and an Activity view of mentions/reactions/thread replies.
how: Configured in Preferences > Notifications; badges appear for DMs, keywords, mentions, app notifications, thread replies, Slack Connect invites, overdue reminders; Windows taskbar flash and notification-area behaviour are separate options.
verevonRelevance: Space needs mention routing and an Activity inbox; Verevon has no mention notifications and no cross-room unread counts.

name: Global push-style hotkeys: toggle mute and command centre, registered on demand by the web app
what: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space mutes a huddle from any app and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K summons the command centre; the web app turns each global shortcut on or off per feature.
how: sr map {toggle_mute: CommandOrControl+Shift+Space, desktop_command_center: CommandOrControl+Shift+K}; TOGGLE_GLOBAL_SHORTCUTS_HANDLER(feature, enabled) registers/unregisters with globalShortcut; on press the shell raises the main window if no window is focused (ar for command centre, at for others) and sends NOTIFY_GLOBAL_SHORTCUTS_TRIGGER(feature). The command-centre one is also gated by the desktop_command_center flag.
evidence: https://slack.com/help/articles/201374536-Slack-keyboard-shortcuts (DOC: Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles huddle mute; Ctrl+Shift+H start/join/leave huddle)
verevonRelevance: A global "mute / ask my agent" shortcut is cheap and loved by power users; keep it opt-in and feature-registered.
notes: DOC page does not mention global shortcuts; this is shell-level only.

name: Low-level key combos with key-down/key-up events and double-tap modifiers (push-to-talk capable)
what: The shell can listen to arbitrary key combinations (up to 8 keys) system-wide and report separate press and release, and to double-press of a modifier key (Cmd, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win).
how: slack-desktop-utils accelerator.registerCombo(keys[], {onKeyDown,onKeyUp}) and registerDoublePressShortcut(modifier, cb, {threshold default 300 ms}) using a single native keyboard hook/event tap (macOS NSEvent monitors, Windows low-level hook); main exposes ACCELERATOR_* IPC with Joi schemas (keys: integers 0+, 1-8 items), disposes handles when the sender is destroyed or crashes; checkAccessibilityPermissions reports {granted, canPrompt} on macOS; native diagnostics include tapDisabledCount stats.
evidence: REA ev_2a90444feeb793611259f458eb756194e4f6f2766a044417716bf34a9f2ec0e8 (inspect_pe_resources slackdesktoputils.node: PE32+ x64, one RT_MANIFEST)
verevonRelevance: Press-and-hold voice capture for a Verevon agent (push-to-talk) needs exactly this primitive; do it natively with strict schemas.
notes: Push-to-talk use is INF from keydown/keyup design; native export names (getComboTapStats, tapDisabledByUserInputCount) read from the .node strings.

name: Native screen-share border overlay (WindowBorderPanel) that follows the shared window or screen
what: While sharing, a coloured border is drawn around the shared window or screen so people know what is being broadcast.
how: slack-desktop-utils exposes huddles.WindowBorderPanel (windowNumber, borderWidth, borderColor RGBA, timerIntervalMs, getWindowPositionAndDimensions with DIP conversion); main registers CALLS_SCREEN_SHARE_* IPC (create, show, hide, setWindowOrScreenId, setBorderWidth, setBorderColor, setTimerIntervalMs, getWindowPositionAndDimensions) with schemas; preload exposes window.desktop.callsScreenshare.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon exposes an agent browser/computer view, a persistent "agent is acting here" border is an excellent safety cue.
notes: Naming shows huddles are the call product (namespace huddles).

name: Screen/window picker thumbnails that exclude Slack's own windows
what: The share dialog gets small previews of screens and windows, never including Slack's notification pop-ups or windows marked as excluded from sharing.
how: GET_SCREEN_PREVIEW_THUMBNAILS clamps thumbnails to 480 px, calls desktopCapturer.getSources(types screen|window), filters sources whose mediaSourceId belongs to windows with excludeFromScreenShare or the notifications window; window state also reports isContentProtected.
verevonRelevance: Protect sensitive Verevon surfaces (approval cards, secrets) with content protection during screen share.

name: Media-permission probing in a utility process with timeout and cache
what: Checking camera/microphone/screen permission cannot freeze the app: it runs in a child process with a 2-second timeout and caches the answer.
how: getMediaAccessStatusViaChildProcess forks utilityProcess (serviceName slack-media-access-check) running systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus; timeout 2000 ms falls back to the main-process value; results cached 4 h (30 s for fallback answers) with forceRefresh; telemetry desktop_media_access_{cached,fresh,force_refresh}.
verevonRelevance: Same isolation pattern would protect a Verevon host from hangs in OS APIs.

name: Audio device enumeration, device init checks and macOS voice-isolated capture
what: Settings can list audio devices with details, test whether a device can be opened (Windows), read the microphone mode, and use system voice isolation on macOS; virtual cameras are stubbed to an empty list.
how: IPC ENUMERATE_AUDIO_DEVICES, GET_AUDIO_DEVICE_DETAILS(index,direction), CAN_INIT_AUDIO_DEVICE(deviceName) -> systemPreferences.canInitAudioDeviceWin, GET_MICROPHONE_MODE; native audio.startVoiceIsolatedCapture with a GC finalizer safety net that stops the capture handle; GET_VIRTUAL_CAMERAS returns [].
verevonRelevance: Relevant only if Verevon adds voice rooms; note the explicit device-open probe to catch exclusive-mode failures.

name: Power-save blocker whose lifetime is tied to a MessagePort
what: While a call or huddle is active the app keeps the machine awake, and the block is released automatically if the renderer drops the handle or crashes.
how: Renderer posts POWER_SAVE_BLOCKER_START with a MessageChannel port; main validates type (prevent-app-suspension|prevent-display-sleep), starts powerSaveBlocker, replies with the id, and stops it when the port closes; POWER_SAVE_BLOCKER_IS_STARTED queries it.
verevonRelevance: Tie any keep-awake for long agent runs to a handle that self-releases; avoids leaked sleep blocks.

name: Call window teardown signals and a 9-sound call sound pack
what: The shell can tell the web app to close the call window or that child windows are closing, and ships ring, join, leave and alert sounds.
how: main->renderer IPC CLOSE_CALL and CLOSING_CHILD_WINDOWS mapped to desktopDelegate.closeCall / onClosingChildWindows; mp3 files calls_incoming_ring_v2, calls_outgoing_ring_v2, calls_alert_v2, calls_confirmation_v2, calls_pop_v2, calls_they_joined_call_v2, calls_they_left_call_v2, calls_you_joined_call_v2, calls_you_left_call_v2.
verevonRelevance: Audible join/leave cues matter for voice rooms; low priority.
notes: Playback code is in the remote web client.

name: Stealth restart: the web app can veto a silent background restart while a huddle or upload is running
what: The shell can ask the web app whether a restart (for example to apply an update) is safe; the app answers yes, or no with a reason: huddle, upload or guard.
how: QUERY_STEALTH_RESTART_SAFE (main -> renderer, with requestId) and STEALTH_RESTART_SAFE_RESPONSE {requestId, safe, reason huddle|upload|guard}; window.desktopDelegate.queryStealthRestartSafe handles it. The STEALTH_RESTART epic body is empty in this build (feature stubbed).
verevonRelevance: Agent runs and approvals in flight should veto updates/restarts the same way; expose a "safe to restart" contract.
notes: Medium: protocol present, orchestration epic is empty in 4.52.178.

name: Recording indicator carried to the tray
what: When any workspace reports an active recording, the tray state shows it.
how: Team state field isRecording (web app -> shell schema); tray state computed by ix(teams) = some team isRecording === true and passed to the tray icon logic.
verevonRelevance: Surface "an agent/meeting is recording or acting" in OS chrome for transparency.
notes: Which feature sets isRecording (huddle recording, clips) is not determined.

name: DOC: huddle capabilities and limits (screen share, drawing, AI notes, captions, participants)
what: Huddles run in any channel or DM on desktop, mobile and supported browsers; two people can share screens at once, desktop users can draw on shared screens, AI notes produce a canvas with transcript embedded, live captions are English only.
how: Free plan 2 participants; paid up to 50 with 25 on video; AI notes are off by default, announced to all participants and cannot be used with externals/guests; transcripts are in the notes canvas and excluded from search; system audio sharing added June 2026.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no calls; if added, copy "everyone is notified when AI notes start" and exclude externals by default.
notes: Search-summary based; one fetch of the huddles help URL returned 404.

name: Hardened BrowserWindow factory with runtime enforcement
what: Every Slack window is created with renderer sandboxing on and Node access off; developers cannot weaken it by accident, and any window that somehow lacks it is destroyed.
how: Frozen webPreferences {nodeIntegration:false, nodeIntegrationInWorker:false, nodeIntegrationInSubFrames:false, contextIsolation:true, sandbox:true, webviewTag:false, autoplayPolicy:"no-user-gesture-required"} are merged last by o3(), which logs an error if the caller tried to override a key; app.enableSandbox() is called globally; a browser-window-created listener inspects getLastWebPreferences() and destroys windows with sandbox or contextIsolation false.
verevonRelevance: Make secure defaults non-overridable in the host factory and add a runtime assertion; the same applies to any Verevon agent-browser window.
notes: Quality 5: defence in depth (factory + global + runtime check). REA saw 0 explicit_web_preferences (factory indirection), so this comes from reading.

name: IPC security gate: frame/process validation, origin allowlist per session, schema per channel, failure beacon
what: Every message from a web page to the shell is checked for who sent it and what it contains; malformed or out-of-context calls are dropped and reported.
how: ipcMain.handle/on wrappers sh/sm/sg: require senderFrame, processId and frameId, reject events whose frame/process changed after navigation ("process transition"/"frame transition"), accept only https Slack-domain origins (or the dev URL) for the main session and only app: origins for the component session; then validate each argument with a per-channel Joi schema (map su, 136 channel entries) padding missing required args; failures call trackValidationFailure {ipc_channel, ipc_sender, ipc_error} which POSTs to the /beacon/ssbipc endpoint.
verevonRelevance: Best template for Verevon gateway-to-host calls: origin + frame + schema + telemetry on every channel, deny by default.
notes: Quality 5. REA counted 4 sender-validation observations and could not enumerate the channels; the 136-entry schema map was read directly.

name: Native bridge only for trusted origins; child windows get one flag; process object trimmed
what: Pages outside Slack's own https domains (or windows opened by them) do not get window.desktop at all; even trusted pop-ups only get a tiny object.
how: The preload checks the URL (https on port 443 and a Slack domain, or the app:// pages) before building the bridge, otherwise exposes only a stub {window}; window.process is reduced to versions, mas and sandboxed; the child preload exposes only slackPlatform.isWayland when the opener is trusted; a Sentry IPC bridge (__SENTRY_IPC__) is exposed in component windows.
evidence: REA ev_546b8e0f18081c29bee0272c77978cdf603b47562901ea61f62066d6c8565cb1 (trace_application_feature api exposeInMainWorld: no-match, partial graph)
verevonRelevance: Never expose host APIs to origins other than the product's own; Verevon's Space SPA should receive a minimal, versioned host object.
notes: REA trace for exposeInMainWorld returned no-match on a partial graph; the exposure sites were found by grep.

name: Navigation, redirect and external-link policy with scheme allowlist and per-host consent
what: Slack windows cannot be navigated to arbitrary sites; links to other sites open in the OS browser, and unusual protocols (ftp, sftp, ssh, smb) show a consent page with a remember option.
how: will-navigate and will-redirect (main frame) allow only trusted hosts, otherwise preventDefault and load app://error (or destroy a child); slack: URLs from the page are routed into the deep-link handler; openExternal allows http/https/mailto/skype/spotify/live/callto/tel/im/sip/sips/slack and devtools schemes; others require a per-hostname allowance stored in settings (allowedHostnames); fallback opener spawns RunDll32 URL.dll,FileProtocolHandler with a scrubbed environment.
verevonRelevance: Agent browsing proposals executed by Quarry need the same allowlist + consent ladder; do not let model-proposed URLs navigate trusted windows.

name: Permission request/check handlers: trusted-origin only, narrow exceptions
what: Cameras, microphones, notifications and other web permissions are granted only to Slack's own origins; fullscreen and sanitized clipboard writes have narrow exceptions.
how: setPermissionRequestHandler and setPermissionCheckHandler on the main and component sessions call y0(): allow when the requesting origin is a trusted Slack host (blob: unwrapped), fullscreen on any https, clipboard-read / fullscreen / clipboard-sanitized-write when the main frame is a recognised Slack window; app://resources/ gets clipboard-sanitized-write; all decisions are logged with origins redacted/normalised; setting isClipboardReadDisabled can switch clipboard read off.
